A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hyper-GCN research, with matching titles and authors. All nine pages of each were inspected, including equations, tables, figures and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; the available material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hyper-GCN recognition results on NTU-60, NTU-120 and NW-UCLA, component ablations, computational costs and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, uniform versus non-uniform hyper-graph experiments, virtual-joint and loss ablations, and standard/lightweight model comparisons.

M1.justification: Within the retained K-nearest incidence construction and eight-branch framework, v2 replaces per-branch weight projection with channel attention across heads, changes hyper-graph normalization and divergence-loss scaling, and specifies manually connecting virtual joints to all physical joints. The default final-stage width increases from 256 to 512. These substantive changes go beyond renaming AHC/MS-HGC to A-NHG/M-HGC.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate skeleton-based action recognition on NTU-60, NTU-120 and NW-UCLA. The added ablations and action visualizations use retained coverage; they introduce no new dataset, task, population or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: Table I adds BlockGCN, Hyper-GNN, Selective-HCN and DST-HCN, while removing ST-GCN, 2s-AGCN, DGNN, SGN, DC-GCN+ADG, DDGCN and MS-G3D. v2's complexity comparison additionally includes DSTA-Net, IIP-Transformer and SkateFormer. This substantially changes the evaluated comparator set, particularly through direct hyper-graph and Transformer comparisons.

E3.justification: The default evaluated architecture changes from 128/256/256 to 128/256/512 channels, with a separate lightweight configuration added. Table II replaces single/multiple-scale settings with uniform/non-uniform controls across K=3,5,7,9,11; Table III crosses virtual-joint counts with loss and M-HGC conditions. Table I also changes InfoGCN's reported modalities. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the single-versus-multiple-scale study with uniform-versus-non-uniform construction analysis and expands virtual-joint testing to quantify divergence-loss effects. It removes the dense-connection ablation and per-class scale-accuracy analysis, adds action-specific hyper-edge case studies, and introduces a standard/lightweight complexity analysis. Figure 6 retains the previous output-feature projections while dropping the input-feature panels.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Recognition results remain point estimates; the similarity heatmaps do not provide uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table I replaces the four-stream accuracy entries: NTU-60 changes from 93.1/96.7 to 93.4/97.1, NTU-120 from 90.2/91.4 to 90.5/91.7, and NW-UCLA from 96.6 to 97.1. The revised architecture prevents treating these as same-setting gains. Numerous ablation entries are replaced, and the lightweight model adds NTU-120 results of 90.4/91.5. v2 Table III contains an unresolved inconsistency: 84.8 is marked as a 2.1-point gain over 84.7.

T1.justification: Equation 6 changes one-sided degree normalization to symmetric normalization with Dv^(-1/2) on both sides. Equations 12–13 redefine the cosine matrix and change the divergence-loss denominator from (Vh-1)^2 to Vh(Vh-1), with explicit removal of self-similarity. These are substantive but localized mathematical revisions; neither version contains a theorem/proof framework.

C1.justification: v2 refines the primary contribution from hyper-graph aggregation versus ordinary graphs toward adaptive non-uniform topology versus fixed hyper-graphs. The conclusion emphasizes A-NHG/M-HGC instead of multi-scale convolution and dense connections. The recognition objective, virtual-joint contribution and broad state-of-the-art claim across three datasets remain.

C2.justification: The mechanism discussion shifts from complementary spatial scales and stage-dependent dense connections to action-dependent non-uniform joint combinations, supported by new interpretations of individual action visualizations. v2 also discusses the accuracy–complexity tradeoff from channel width. The earlier dense-connection variance explanation and local-versus-global motion interpretation of scale selection are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents the revised channel-attention mappings, activations and standard/lightweight channel widths. However, it removes training batch sizes of 64/16, explicit dataset split descriptions and the ablation-baseline construction recipe. The RTX 3090, optimizer, 140-epoch budget and learning-rate schedule remain documented; no code-access information is added.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand discussion of Transformer topology, feature representations and computational cost, while sharpening positioning against fixed hyper-graphs. Added references include BlockGCN, IGFormer, STST, STTFormer, SkateFormer and squeeze-and-excitation; 3MFormer and Skeleton Mixformer references disappear. IIP-Transformer was already cited in v1, but receives substantive discussion and evaluation in v2.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, related work and method narrative, redistributing pooling and weight construction between Sections III-C and III-D. It changes module terminology, substantially condenses architecture and dataset descriptions, and reorganizes the experimental discussion around revised ablations and a new complexity subsection.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 are substantially redrawn. Figure 4 replaces a class-accuracy bar chart with temporal skeleton visualizations, and Figure 6 contracts from four panels to two retained output projections. Tables I–III receive new grouping or comparison structures, while Table IV changes from architecture ablations to performance/complexity comparisons.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for its central design through direct hyper-graph baselines, uniform/non-uniform controls, quantitative divergence-loss ablations and standard/lightweight comparisons. These address gaps in v1's evidence more directly than higher accuracy alone. The gain is limited by lost batch-size, split and baseline details, plus numerical inconsistencies such as Table III's 84.8 result labeled as a 2.1-point improvement over 84.7.
